statement: Let $f(x)=\\frac{1-x}{1+x}$ for $x\\neq -1$. (i) Show that $f(f(x))=x$. (ii) Deduce that $f$ is its own inverse. (iii) Find the range of $f$ on its domain.
solution: (i) $f(f(x))=\\frac{1-\\frac{1-x}{1+x}}{1+\\frac{1-x}{1+x}}=\\frac{\\frac{(1+x)-(1-x)}{1+x}}{\\frac{(1+x)+(1-x)}{1+x}}=\\frac{2x}{2}=x$. (ii) Since $f(f(x))=x$ for all $x\\neq -1$, we have $f^{-1}=f$; $f$ is self-inverse. (iii) From $y=\\frac{1-x}{1+x}$ we get $y(1+x)=1-x$, so $x(y+1)=1-y$ and $x=\\frac{1-y}{1+y}$, which requires $y\\neq -1$. Hence the range is $\\mathbb{R}\\setminus\\{-1\\}$.
hints: Compare with the definition of an inverse.
